title: swing-window-priority-decoupler-for-continuous-batcher
author: Ethan Chen
release_notes: Improves continuous batcher fairness and starvation resistance for mixed KV/cache and non-cache workloads. Adds new metrics for per-tenant admission skew and a rollout plan to slowly enable the decoupler.
body: Motivation: Continuous batching has been effective at improving throughput but suffers intermittent starvation and unfair admission when workloads mix KV-hot requests with variable token-cost requests. Existing fixes (deadline smoothing, slot reservations) reduced tail but did not address rapid swing behavior where a tenant or model transiently dominates admission and evicts other queued groups. This PR introduces the 'swing window priority decoupler'—a lightweight admission layer that decouples slot assignment from strict queue position to smooth sudden swings while preserving throughput and SLOs.Design summary: The decoupler maintains a short 'swing window' (configurable time horizon) per queue-class that tracks recent admission deltas and KV cache hotness signals. When the window detects a sudden positive swing (large short-term gain in admissions) it applies a soft dampening multiplier to that class's immediate admission quota and credits neighboring classes with proportionate soft-credits so they can be admitted sooner. Key heuristics are preserved: latency-sensitive requests still get priority via deadline buckets, and KV-pin-heavy requests are recognized by propagated kernel hints (kv_hot=true) so we avoid penalizing legitimate cache-warm handoffs. Implementation notes: - New runtime component: scheduler/decoupler/swing_window.go (Go) implements the time-decayed admission counters, dampening multiplier, and credit ledger. - Admission path changes: runtime/batcher/continuous_admitter.go integrates decoupler decisions; admission now consults decoupler.allowedFor(class, estimateTokenCost, kvHint). - Kernel hint propagation: runtime/kernel/hints.rs updated to serialize kv_hot and estimated_compute_cost so the scheduler can consider them without reading model internals. - Metrics and observability: metrics/swing_window_instrumentation.{go,md} adds per-tenant swing_delta, swing_suppressed, credit_issued, and decoupler_latency histograms. - Tests: unit tests for decoupler logic and integration tests in perf/continuous_bench that replay mixed KV-hot and token-heavy traces. - Docs: docs/ops/continuous-batcher-tuning.md includes rollout guidance and knobs. Behavior details: - Swing window length defaults to 200ms, configurable per-deployment. - Dampening multiplier clamps to [0.5,1.0] to avoid starving high-throughput classes. - Credit issuance is bounded to 15% of current window capacity to prevent over-correction. - If KV-hotness is high and the request is a cache-priming path, the decoupler biases toward allowing admission to preserve warm caches. Benchmarks: Microbench harness (perf/continuous_bench) ran three representative workloads: mixed-echo (even), bursty-kv (70% kv-hot bursts), and token-skew (50% token-heavy long sequences). Results vs main (averaged over 30 runs): - P50 latency: unchanged +/- 3% - P95 latency: reduced by 8% on bursty-kv - P99 latency: reduced by 21% on mixed bursts - Throughput: sustained within 2% of main in steady state - Starvation incidents (classification where queued groups waited >2s): main=14 incidents, swing-decoupler=2 incidents Safety and rollout: - Feature gate: runtime.flags.enable_swing_decoupler=false by default for now. - Canary plan: enable for 5% of traffic, monitor swing_suppressed and credit_issued, then ramp to 50% over 48h if P99 and throughput stable. - Fallback: if decoupler_latency > 1ms median or P99 increases, auto-disable on the host. Review conversation (summary): - Maya Lin: requested clearer invariants around credit bounds and asked for additional tests covering extreme swings. Author response: added bounded-credit tests and microbench scenarios that drive 10x swings. - Arjun Kapoor: asked whether the dampening multiplier could cause underutilization on short bursts; author added an adaptive decay that reduces suppression if window utilization is low. - Sofia Martinez: requested better telemetry for tenant-level debugging; author added tenant-tagged metrics and a quick query in docs for incident triage. - Liam O'Reilly: pointed out potential race between admission path and in-flight kernel hint refresh; patch added an atomic snapshot of hints to the admission decision. CI and flakiness: initial CI run had a flaky integration test due to timing in perf harness; fixed by using deterministic clocks in tests. All checks passing on final run. Files changed (high level): - runtime/batcher/continuous_admitter.go - scheduler/decoupler/swing_window.go - scheduler/decoupler/swing_window_test.go - runtime/kernel/hints.rs - metrics/swing_window_instrumentation.go - perf/continuous_bench/replays/mixed_burst.yaml - perf/continuous_bench/bench_runner.go - docs/ops/continuous-batcher-tuning.md - config/flags.yaml - integration/recorder/deterministic_clock.go - CHANGELOG.md Migration notes: No on-disk state changes. The only compatibility surface is the serialized kernel hint payload; a runtime guard keeps old kernels compatible. Follow-ups: - ENG-2794: explore ML-driven adaptive multipliers based on long tail prediction. - ENG-2795: expose per-tenant swing credits in the Redwood Console. - Small refactor: unify decoupler and slot-reserver to share credit ledger. Conclusion: This PR reduces starvation risk for mixed workloads while preserving throughput and adds operational visibility to understand transient swings. The default is gated and the rollout plan is conservative. Merge outcome: squash-merged into main on 2024-12-02.

review_comments: Maya Lin: Please add bounded-credit tests and show behaviour under extreme swings. - Addressed in swing_window_test.go
Arjun Kapoor: Concerned about underutilization on short bursts; can dampening adapt? - Added adaptive decay and documentation
Sofia Martinez: Need tenant-level metrics for triage. - Added tenant tags to swing_suppressed & credit_issued
Liam O'Reilly: Potential race on kernel hint refresh. - Snapshotting implemented and tested
perf_summary: P95 decreased by 8% on bursty-kv; P99 decreased by 21% on mixed bursts; throughput steady within 2% of baseline; starvation incidents reduced from 14 to 2 in replay tests.
notes: Feature is behind a flag and will be canaried. No breaking changes. Kernel hint serialization is backward compatible via versioned payloads.
changelog_entry: swing window priority decoupler: reduces queueing starvation in continuous batcher for mixed KV and token-cost workloads; gated rollout.
guidance: Operators: start with enable_swing_decoupler=false. Canary via traffic-split to 5% and monitor metrics: swing_suppressed, credit_issued, decoupler_latency, p99_latency. Ramp only if decoupler_latency < 1ms median and p99 stable.
